For administrators

Process Mining — Administration
Setup & Operations Guide

A guided tour of the Administration interface, tab by tab, in roughly the order you would set up a new installation — users and roles, database connections, TLS, sign-in security, logging, backups and the optional surfaces.

The Administration site is where the whole installation is configured. It is a separate surface from the application, reachable only by administrators, and it controls the app, the Integration console and the Action Designer as well as itself.
1

Sign in & the dashboard

Open the Administration interface in your browser (by default on port 8090) and sign in with an administrator account. Only administrators can reach this site — a correct password on a non-admin account is refused with the same message as a wrong one. The dashboard opens on App Control, with every tab along the top.

NoteOn first run a banner reminds you to change the default administrator password — do that on day one.
2

App Control — licence & restart

The App Control tab shows the licence status and, in Demo Mode, a one-time grace countdown. Upload a signed licence here. The ↻ Restart button re-binds all browser surfaces at once — use it after a TLS change or after enabling/disabling a feature.

3

TLS / SSL

Choose how the site is served: off (HTTP), optional (HTTP + HTTPS) or required (HTTPS only). Generate a self-signed certificate or upload your own, then activate it. A single restart applies the mode and certificate to the app, admin, integration and Actions surfaces together.

NoteThe admin interface follows the same TLS mode, so a bad certificate can lock you out — keep a way back in (e.g. the HTTP fallback) until you have verified the new one.
4

Users & sign-in

Add user accounts and grant roles: Power user, Developer and Administrator (an account with none is a standard user). Here you also control the global require sign-in switch, the idle timeout, the failed-login lockout, and per-account passkeys and two-factor (with master toggles and a force-enrolment option). A badge marks each account local or LDAP.

NoteRoles are never granted by the directory — every role is set explicitly here. Keep at least one local administrator as break-glass access.
5

Database Connections

Create the database connections your users will analyse: name, host, port, schema and credentials, plus an optional AI model server. Assign each connection to the users who may use it — a user only ever sees their assigned connections. Test checks the values before saving. You can also opt a connection into pre-materialised transitions for faster maps.

6

Directory (LDAP / Active Directory)

Optionally let the main app accept directory sign-ins via search + bind: set the server URI, service-account bind DN/password, base DN, user filter and attributes, then test a login. Directory users are created locally on first sign-in as plain accounts you then grant roles to. Two switches let you also allow directory sign-in to this admin interface, and show or hide the Authentication Server availability indicator on the login panels.

7

Logging

The Logging tab is a filterable audit trail: sign-ins, configuration changes, certificate and connection actions, backups and more, each tagged by operation so you can narrow to exactly what you need. The live log is kept in a database; older segments rotate to files.

8

Backup & restore

Export an encrypted backup of the security store on demand, or schedule automatic backups on a cron expression with a retention count. Backups are password-protected; the same password restores them. Inspect a backup before restoring it.

NoteEnabling a schedule requires a password — it is never echoed back, so store it safely.
9

Customize the login panels

Set the look of every sign-in panel: a solid background colour or an uploaded image, shared by the app, admin, integration and Actions surfaces. The freely-editable version line (e.g. “V0.95 – Milford Sound”) also appears under the title.

10

The other surfaces & reporting

Two more tabs turn optional surfaces on or off: Integration (the data-source console for developers) and Actions (the Action Designer, off by default). Both take effect after a restart. The Reporting tab configures the AI report per connection and project — its letterhead, logo and sections, and the analysis prompt.

NoteEnabling or disabling a surface only flips a flag; press ↻ Restart on App Control to bind or release its listener.

Day-one checklist

  1. Change the default administrator password (banner on App Control).
  2. Choose a TLS mode and activate a certificate.
  3. Create at least one database connection and assign it to the right users.
  4. Keep one local administrator account as break-glass access.
  5. Set an idle timeout and a failed-login lockout that match your policy.
  6. Schedule encrypted backups.
